newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian stocks stable as investors sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Estonian stocks stable as investors sidelined.

text.p: Estonian stock market trade on Thursday was stable with investors contemplating their positions and staying on the sidelines for the moment, dealers said.
The Tallinn stock exchange index firmed 0.15 percent to close at 187.10 on a turnover of 34.3 million kroons on the official list.
Union Bank was the most active registering a trade of 8.2 million kroons to ease by 0.15 kroons to 38.90.
It earlier forecast a 1997 profit of 105.8 million kroons after 57 million in 1995.
The 1997 profit includes the contribution of North Estonian Bank, with which Union Bank is to merge.

"People who bought Union bank at a higher price wanted to get out and look for a quicker return. They hoped that the results would raise the price, but the selling pressure was too strong and they sold anyway," said a trader.
Hansapank turned over 7.4 million kroons of shares to close 0.75 kroons down at 176.25.
Forekspank was up 1.60 kroons to finish on 149.75 with a turnover of 6.6 million kroons.
In other stocks, Savings Bank also strengthened to finish 0.95 kroons stronger on 90.45 with a trade of 4.7 million kroons.
Tallinna Pank was not very active, and continued to slide to close 1.05 kroons lower at 62.45 on trade of 3.5 million kroons.
It is still suffering from a newspaper report which said it was making big losses from a loan to a shipping line.

"Tallinna Pank shareholders are still divided on what to do. Most are waiting for the audited results of the company to get an accurate picture of the bank's exposure to the shipping loan," said an analyst.
The over-the-counter market was again quiet with only 4.1 million kroons of shares traded.
Rakvere meat plant turned over two million kroons of shares to firm by 0.40 to 15.15 kroons.
